simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Judges, 1 Samuel, Ezra, Nehemiah, Psalms, beginning at Judges 4:2. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship.

simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows סִיסְרָא through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

They told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam was gone up to Mount Tabor.
Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles, to the river Kishon.

Deborah said to Barak, “Go; for this is the day in which Yahweh has delivered Sisera into your hand. Hasn’t Yahweh gone out before you?” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

However Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, “Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; don’t be afraid.” He came in to her into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.

definitions.short: Sisera , the name of a Canaanitish king and of one of the Nethinim
definitions.full: H5516. Sisera סִיסְרָא 21 proper name, masculine (GFM Judg 4:2 ; PAOS xix (1898), 160 compare Hittite names in +? ); — 1 general of Jabin, king of Hazor Judg 4:2 12 t. Judges 4; apparently himself king 5:20 , 26 , 28 , 30 ; compare 1Sam 12:9 ; Psa 83:10 ; — on ׳ס see GFM Ju, 107 ff.; PAOS 1.c. ; ᵐ5 Σ ( ε ) ισαρα . 2 בְּנֵיסִֿיסְרָא returned exiles, Ezra 2:53 = Neh 7:55 ; ᵐ5 Σεισαραθ , Σισαρα , etc.
